name: Random Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity of Addressing
proof: Restrict here to $n=2^r$ with all r-bit words present, so $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor=\log_2n=r$. Random proper equivalence-query complexity is at least random equivalence-query complexity, whose established addressing value is $\lfloor\log n\rfloor$. It is at most log size, also $\lfloor\log n\rfloor$. Hence equality holds.
details: Scope: complete-code subfamily $n=2^r$, $r\ge1$. The displayed formula is not asserted for arbitrary injective encodings at other n.
